newsitem.title: BRAZIL: IFC to support Brazil privatization program - paper.
newsitem.headline: IFC to support Brazil privatization program - paper.

text.p: The World Bank-affiliated International Finance Corporation (IFC) wants to give financial support to Brazil's privatization program in the infrastructure sector, a newspaper said.

Brazil, which received the second largest amount of funds allocated by the IFC between June 1995 and June 1996, could take the first place as the country's privatization program moves into the infrastructure sector, Gazeta Mercantil said.

The IFC representative in Brazil, Bruce Leighton, said 1997 was critical for the privatization of the infrastructure sector and the success of the program depended on the access to long-term financing, according to Gazeta.

"We think the IFC is well-positioned to provide part of this financing with its own resources and funds from international banks in the form of consortia," Gazeta quoted Leighton as saying. Brazil received $328 million in IFC loans and direct investments out of a total of $3.2 billion awarded to 68 countries. Only Argentina received more in the 1995/96 period.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
